Dear Hiring Manager,

I am applying for the Internal Sales Consultant role on State Street Investment Management's US Wealth team in Boston. You describe a role that partners with Regional Consultants to grow business with broker-dealer and RIA clients through outreach by phone, email and video. I am moving into sales from finance, and your posting is one of the few that ties sales to the investment knowledge I have built.

I hold a B.S. in Finance from Suffolk and an M.A. in International Economics and Finance from Brandeis, where I studied Corporate Finance and Advanced Finance. I know the Bloomberg Terminal. As Financial Manager at AMG Family Dental in Belmont, I also see the buyer's side of money decisions. I build the annual operating budget and monthly forecasts, and I report variances and KPIs to ownership.

The sales skills I can point to are persistence and follow-up. I identified and recovered more than $500K in annual revenue by chasing underpaid claims, and I reduced A/R aging by 10% by tightening insurance claim follow-up. At Northrop Grumman I presented cost-saving recommendations to senior leadership, and at FYND in Tokyo I presented AI adoption recommendations to the co-founders, so I am used to explaining ideas to senior people.

I should be direct about the gap. I have no formal sales experience, and your posting prefers two to four years in investment management, wealth management or financial services, with SIE, Series 7 and 63 licenses held or obtained within six months of starting. I do not hold those licenses yet, but I am willing to sit for them on your timeline. I live near Boston, I am a US citizen, and I am available immediately.

Sincerely,
Alexander Airapetian
